title: Bug Bounty Cluster Hunting & Vulnerability Chains (A -> B -> C)

chains.name: IDOR Escalation to Full Account Takeover

step_a.action: Inspect response body for sensitive identifiers: email, phone, security question, tenant ID

step_b.finding: PUT /api/v1/users/{id} accepts email/phone update without verifying current password or ownership
step_b.action: Swap attacker email onto victim user ID

step_c.finding: Password reset triggered to attacker email

chains.name: SSRF Cloud Metadata to Remote Code Execution

step_a.finding: SSRF parameter in PDF generator or webhook URL input

step_b.finding: Retrieve AWS IAM role temporary keys (AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, Token)
step_b.action: Verify privileges via aws sts get-caller-identity and check ec2/lambda/s3 permissions

step_c.finding: Use IAM permissions to update AWS Lambda function or EC2 user-data script

chains.name: Open Redirect to OAuth Code Theft (ATO)

step_a.action: Supply target redirect into primary OAuth authorization URL redirect_uri

step_b.finding: OAuth provider permits whitelisted domain subdirectory without strict exact-path matching
step_b.action: Victim clicks authorization link: browser follows open redirect carrying ?code=AUTHORIZATION_CODE

step_c.finding: Attacker captures authorization code on external server and exchanges for victim access token
step_c.impact: Account Takeover via OAuth token exfiltration

chains.name: CORS Misconfiguration to Authenticated Data Theft

step_b.finding: Craft cross-origin fetch() script hosted on attacker.com
step_b.action: Victim visits attacker page with active session cookies

step_c.finding: Response containing private banking/PII details is read and sent to attacker server
step_c.impact: Mass PII and financial record exfiltration
